findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 50 mm is observed in the head of the pancreas. Serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion are noted. There is contact of more than 180° with the portal vein, suggesting invasion. No invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum is observed. No other local invasion factors are identified. Lymph node metastasis is observed in one node at station 8p. No other evident metastases are observed.

responses.content:
Task 1: Diagnose the local invasion factors of pancreatic cancer.

CH0 (no invasion of the common hepatic artery)
DU0 (no invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum)
S1 (serosal invasion)
RP1 (retropancreatic tissue invasion)
PV1 (invasion of the portal vein)
A0 (no invasion of the abdominal aorta)
PL0 (no invasion of the pancreatic lymphatic vessels)
OO1 (contact of more than 180° with the portal vein, suggesting invasion)

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the image findings, the tumor is 50 mm in size and has invaded the serosa, retropancreatic tissue, and portal vein. The size-based criteria (T1a, T1b, T1c) are not met, as the tumor is 50 mm, which is larger than the maximum size for T1a (2 cm) and T1b (5 cm). The extension-based criteria (T3, T4) are met, as the tumor has invaded the serosa and retropancreatic tissue. Therefore, the T classification is T3.

Task 3: Determine the N classification of pancreatic cancer.

The regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer are:
- Station 8p (left gastric artery lymph nodes)
- Station 8a (common hepatic artery lymph nodes)
- Station 9 (proper hepatic artery lymph nodes)
- Station 12a (left pancreaticoduodenal artery lymph nodes)
- Station 12b (right pancreaticoduodenal artery lymph nodes)
- Station 13 (transverse pancreatic duct lymph nodes)

The patient's metastatic lymph node station is 8p, which is regional. There is only one metastatic lymph node at station 8p. Therefore, the N classification is N1a.

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

There is no evidence of distant metastases, such as to non-regional lymph nodes or distant organs. Therefore, the M classification is M0.

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the results of Task 1 and Task 4, the tumor has invaded the serosa and portal vein, but there is no evidence of distant metastasis. Therefore, the resectability classification is Resectable (R).

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

Based on the determined T (T3), N (N1a), and M (M0) categories, the overall stage is Stage IIA.
